items.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995…
items.q: it features ten piano players — Hank Jones, John Lewis, Kenny Barron, Ray Bryant, Gene Harris, Joanne Brackeen, Roger Kellaway, and who have I left out, oh, Cedar Walton and myself.

ctx.x: Which we have with us today for your autograph.

But I’m contracted to Enja now. And I just got back from Japan on a tour that is called “100 Gold Fingers,” it features ten piano players — Hank Jones, John Lewis, Kenny Barron, Ray Bryant, Gene Harris, Joanne Brackeen, Roger Kellaway, and who have I left out, oh, Cedar Walton and myself. And there was one more. Ten of us.

items.title: Ray Bryant interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998
items.q: Junior and I sort of found ourselves together most of the time, and we played the blues. And so that’s why the Blues Brothers.

ctx.x: A friend of yours, Junior Mance, told me to ask you about the Blues Brothers.

Well within this production, the One Hundred Gold Fingers, you get to play duets, you know you play your solo piano, you play duets with other people. Marian did it once with us, she went over one year. The roster varies, they change it around from year to year. But I’ve been on every one every year, I’ve been on every one, Junior has too. So I guess it was inevitable, in the pairing up of different piano players like playing duets, Junior and I would end up together at least. So we did it once and we played the…
Is it possible to put into words what is so attractive — I don’t know if that’s the right word — but the blues just seems to grab people. Have you ever been able to understand why that is?
